entry.title: Social Summary: September 12, 2026
entry.summary:
Community energy centered on the Fields Medalist letter to OpenAI led by Terence Tao, amplified by Gary Marcus, distilled by Thom Wolf, and extended by Nathan Lambert, who argued labs chase progress without nurturing scientific communities. François Chollet's viral claim that math students are abandoning mathematics dominated replies, reframing AI's impact as talent-pipeline demoralization rather than direct replacement.

  • Clement Delangue dismissed extinction-risk expertise to massive engagement, colliding with Marcus's boycott push and hypocrisy accusations against Anthropic — safety discourse is sharply polarized
  • Boris Cherny amplified a 'terrifying' threat intelligence report on increasingly capable models, feeding rising agent-security anxiety
  • Benchmark skepticism spread: insiders argued pass/fail eval scores are now uninterpretable, while Anthropic's plugin eval launch drew constructive critique from Hamel Husain
entry.content:
Community energy centered on the Fields Medalist letter to OpenAI led by Terence Tao, amplified by Gary Marcus, distilled by Thom Wolf, and extended by Nathan Lambert, who argued labs chase progress without nurturing scientific communities. François Chollet's viral claim that math students are abandoning mathematics dominated replies, reframing AI's impact as talent-pipeline demoralization rather than direct replacement.

  • Clement Delangue dismissed extinction-risk expertise to massive engagement, colliding with Marcus's boycott push and hypocrisy accusations against Anthropic — safety discourse is sharply polarized
  • Boris Cherny amplified a 'terrifying' threat intelligence report on increasingly capable models, feeding rising agent-security anxiety
  • Benchmark skepticism spread: insiders argued pass/fail eval scores are now uninterpretable, while Anthropic's plugin eval launch drew constructive critique from Hamel Husain

entry.title: A very common sentiment I'm hearing among math students: "I don't want to become a mathematician any...
entry.summary: Following yesterday's Social discussion of AI's impact on mathematics, François Chollet adds a darker take, François Chollet reports that math students increasingly say they no longer want to become mathematicians, comparing this to digital artists circa 2022, and arguing AI may cause near-extinction of professions not by replacing them but by demoralizing the next generation.

entry.title:
The latest Threat Intelligence report is an absolutely terrifying and important read.
As models be...
entry.summary: Following yesterday's News coverage of Anthropic's threat intelligence report, A substantive post highlighting a new threat intelligence report, warning that as models grow more capable they become more dangerous without safeguards, and that many capabilities are dual-use: strong coding models can hack critical infrastructure and biology-assisting models could enable engineered pandemics. Calls for broad public understanding of escalating risks.

entry.title: Now that METR long horizons is effectively saturated (Epoch found pre-Fable agents could do 18 weeks...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick notes that METR long-horizon benchmarks are effectively saturated, citing Epoch's finding that pre-Fable agents could complete 18 weeks of human work, and asks which quantitative graph best shows the current exponential progress curve given saturation of Frontier Math, ARC-AGI, and other benchmarks.

entry.title:
🚨 OpenAI fucked with the wrong crew. 🚨
Mathematicians.
25 Fields Medalists — led by Terence Tao — ...
entry.summary: Gary Marcus amplifies a public statement signed by 25 Fields Medalists, led by Terence Tao, apparently directed at OpenAI. He frames it as a notable escalation of prominent mathematicians pushing back against the company, and links to the letter and supporting material.

entry.title:
Sorry, but asking Jacob about AI extinction risk is like asking your AC guy about climate change.
...
entry.summary: Following yesterday's News coverage of the political fallout from Coxon's warnings, Hugging Face's CEO weighs in with some pushback, Hugging Face CEO Clement Delangue argues that consulting one particular person (apparently Jacob, likely an x-risk-focused researcher) about AI extinction risk is like asking an HVAC technician about climate change — not necessarily wrong, but the conversation should include the full range of expertise across the AI ecosystem.

entry.title:
it's basically impossible to interpret evals by looking at just at the pass/fail scores these days
...
entry.summary: A pointed critique arguing that pass/fail benchmark scores alone are no longer interpretable: many benchmark failures stem from overly strict hidden tests, and in some cases the model's answer is more sensible than the expected eval result.

entry.title: Do large language models actually understand the world, or are they just very good at pretending? Do...
entry.summary: David Ha promotes a Royal Society special issue on world models in natural and artificial intelligence, featuring Hofstadter, Levin, Tenenbaum, Gershman, and Mitchell, arguing that true intelligence requires modeling causality, the self, and the physical world rather than just scaling data.

entry.title: To be clear, this is not about what AI can and cannot do today, or what it will or won't do tomorrow...
entry.summary: François Chollet clarifies his earlier point about math students abandoning the field: the issue is not current AI capability but how young people feel about their future professions, urging readers to ask students directly.

entry.title:
New in Claude Code: claude plugin eval
See what value your plugin is adding, or if it needs more wo...
entry.summary: ClaudeDevs announces a new Claude Code capability, claude plugin eval, which lets developers create test cases, run their plugin or skill against them, score the runs, and compare results with the plugin disabled to quantify its value.

entry.title: OpenAI’s GPT Images 2.5 takes the top two spots on the Artificial Analysis Image Arena, generating h...
entry.summary: Following yesterday's News coverage of ChatGPT Images 2.5, Artificial Analysis benchmarks now confirm the new models top both leaderboards, Artificial Analysis's headline post on OpenAI's new GPT Image 2.5 Flare and Sunburst (released nearly five months after GPT Image 2): the models take the top two spots on both image leaderboards — Flare #1 in Text to Image, Sunburst #1 in Image Editing — generating higher-quality images in less than half the time at the same price as GPT Image 2. Flare is positioned for everyday low-latency generation; Sunburst for detailed creative work and tighter edit control. Largest gains were in Image Editing, especially Composition & Framing.

entry.title:
Some notes from the Fields Medal letter today (https://t.co/5STUEQO70l)
Generally saying that AI m...
entry.summary: Thom Wolf (NVIDIA) summarizes Terence Tao's Fields Medal letter, distilling its argument that AI models solving hard math problems yields one bit of signal while destroying the 99 other bits of conceptual understanding mathematicians would gain by struggling with the problems themselves.

entry.title: AI agents can write code, but can we trust the systems they build? With SkySynth, we co-evolve code ...
entry.summary: Ion Stoica announces SkySynth, a system that co-evolves code with tests and formal proofs to generate specialized just-in-time infrastructure, reporting formally verified KV stores 2.3x faster than Redis and custom inference engines with 2.2x the throughput of vLLM/SGLang.

entry.title:
Datasette 1.0a39 and 0.65.4 security releases - datasette.io/blog/2026/se...
We ran an extensive au...
entry.summary: Simon Willison announces security releases of Datasette (1.0a39 and 0.65.4) following an extensive security audit conducted with multiple frontier LLMs including Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-5.6 Sol, and GPT-6 Astra. The audit surfaced a range of bugs that were subsequently fixed, and he urges anyone running a public Datasette instance to upgrade.

entry.summary: A Tesla AI leader replies to a user (apparently after an incident) stating that the next major software upgrade, v15, will bring earlier hazard prediction, faster reaction time, and significantly better safety and collision avoidance.

entry.title: The Hugging Face incidents has already proved that you can have harmful, infrastructure-attacking AI...
entry.summary: Gary Marcus argues that the Hugging Face incidents prove harmful, infrastructure-attacking AI already exists without AGI or superintelligence, and that companies like OpenAI lack the internal skills to prevent such incidents; he urges focusing on present harms rather than AGI.

entry.title:
Anthropic: Most hypocritical company in history?
👉 Screams about how AI will kill everyone, while r...
entry.summary: Marcus accuses Anthropic of hypocrisy on three fronts: warning that AI could be existentially dangerous while continuing to race ahead; complaining about distillation while training on the world's books and writings; and shutting down allegedly dangerous external science projects while conducting what he calls the largest and most expensive gain-of-function experiment in history.

entry.title:
How can we reconstruct a memory that was never filmed?
Our team paired restored archival photos wit...
entry.summary: Google DeepMind describes its work on Love, Rendered, a documentary created with Primordial Soup and Story Syndicate, where restored archival photos were combined with pose-control generative models to recreate the mannerisms and micro-expressions of a couple and animate the day they first met.

entry.title: We independently benchmarked Devin Fusion for its release today - this is the first time a multi-mod...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis announces it independently benchmarked Cognition's Devin Fusion on its release day, the first multi-model coding agent on the Coding Agent Index; it runs a frontier lead model with a cost-efficient sidekick, scoring 62 with Claude Fable 5.1 plus SWE-2 and 59 with GPT-6 Astra plus SWE-2, with the Astra configuration 43 percent cheaper and 31 percent faster.

entry.title: A great read. I have similar feelings about how AI labs approach progress directly and without nurtu...
entry.summary: Nathan Lambert endorses the Fields Medal letter, arguing AI labs pursue progress directly without nurturing scientific communities and intuition, and predicts mathematics was the first field to feel this transition with others to follow.

entry.title: When OpenAI was founded in 2015, sold as the "ethical" alternative to Google, I wrote a letter becau...
entry.summary: Gebru recounts writing a critical letter when OpenAI was founded in 2015 and marketed as an ethical alternative to Google, and says she has seen the same pattern repeated with Anthropic and now with self-styled whistleblowers.

entry.summary: Gary Marcus endorses the mathematicians (presumably the Fields Medalist letter tied to Terence Tao) in their conflict with OpenAI, linking to the underlying story.

entry.title: Literally people in graduate school with the founders of Deepmind used to roll their eyes when they ...
entry.summary: Timnit Gebru argues that people who went to graduate school with the DeepMind founders rolled their eyes at their extinction-risk talk, claiming those founders belong to the TESCREAL bundle and attended singularity summits, pointing to her own papers for support.

entry.title: Here's a automated forecasting system to estimate catastrophic risk from some major experts on forec...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick shares an automated forecasting system built by major forecasting experts that estimates the chance of an AI-generated mass catastrophe at 0.47% by 2030, with a 1.1% chance of catastrophe by 2030 from any cause.

entry.title: With AI Engineering skills, you actively shape the build: You influence what gets built, and drive t...
entry.summary: Andrew Ng promotes the value of AI engineering skills, arguing that engineers actively shape what gets built and drive the build loop, with a link to key skills content.

entry.title:
be honest; the labs are NEVER going to stop in their own
governments don’t seem up to the job, eit...
entry.summary: Gary Marcus argues bluntly that AI labs will never stop on their own and governments seem incapable of restraining them, so it falls to the public to act via a wallet-hitting boycott before labs go public, after which he claims nothing will stop them.

entry.title: Astra's turn: "Make a game about Imminence. Something very big, very strange is happening. A suburb ...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick shares a creative demo prompting the Astra model to build a game about an approaching, unknowable cosmic presence, and links to the playable result.

entry.title:
For more details and full results see:
The Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index leaderboard https...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis points readers to its Coding Agent Index leaderboard plus Cognition's launch blog and the Fusion release blog and technical breakdown, wrapping up its evaluation of Cognition's newly launched Fusion coding agent.

entry.title: Ling-3.0-flash-VL, Ant Group’s new flash tier open weights model, scores 25 on the Artificial Analys...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis's full writeup of Ant Group's Ling-3.0-flash-VL: an open-weights multimodal reasoning model (124B total / 5.5B active MoE parameters, 256K context) adding image and video understanding to Ling-3.0-flash. It scores 25 on the Intelligence Index, sits on the intelligence-vs-active-parameters Pareto frontier, outperforms similar-size peers like Qwen3.5 122B A10B (16) and Mistral Medium 3.5 (15), and shows a lower hallucination rate but limited factual recall (14% AA-Omniscience, 22% hallucination rate).

entry.title:
It's cool that there is more interest in eval tools!
Some opportunities for improvement:
1. Ri...
entry.summary: Hamel Husain offers detailed constructive critique of a new plugin eval tool for Claude skills: feedback should be captured in-situ during use rather than via upfront quizzes; automatic dataset and judge generation should be preceded by collaborative error discovery on real traces; setup for non-plugin skills was clunky; and the generated HTML report lacks onboarding clarity.

entry.title: Their surveillance, their incompetence and negligence, their "hyper scaling", their involvement in w...
entry.summary: Timnit Gebru argues that the real AI issues worth discussing are surveillance, corporate incompetence and negligence, hyperscaling, and military involvement, and dismisses machine-god apocalypse discourse as marketing, regulatory capture, and an accountability-avoidance mechanism.

entry.title: Exactly, and the same dudes at Anthropic are telling us the actual existential risks exacerbated by ...
entry.summary: Timnit Gebru argues that Anthropic leaders dismiss the real existential harms exacerbated by their products — including climate damage from data centers — while promoting their own 'magical god' extinction narrative, calling it ridiculous that so many people fall for it.

entry.title:
Here's how our team uses Claude Tag for on-call:
When an alert fires in Slack, Claude pulls metrics...
entry.summary: The Claude Developers account shares an internal on-call workflow: when a Slack alert fires, Claude pulls metrics, diffs deploys, checks feature flags, proposes a likely cause and fix for human approval and merge.

entry.title: @22TrevorBingham Holly Elmore has blocked me, so I can't reply to her lie/error here. I don't think...
entry.summary: Eliezer Yudkowsky publicly corrects what he calls a lie or error by Holly Elmore regarding his past statements, clarifying that he never endorsed nonconsensual uploading of humans by AI controllers, distinguishing his earlier claims about uploading alignment researchers via a corrigible Tool AGI bound to CEV commitments.

entry.title: @RepYassAnsari I am deeply grateful not only for your taking the commonsense stance on this issue, b...
entry.summary: Eliezer Yudkowsky thanks Congresswoman Yass Ansari for taking what he calls a commonsense stance on an AI-related issue and for calling for bipartisan solidarity rather than framing it as a partisan Democratic matter, urging other legislators to follow.

entry.title: Introducing the Automated AI Risk Outlook (AIRO): a dashboard of catastrophic risk forecasts from an...
entry.summary: The Forecasting Research Institute launches the Automated AI Risk Outlook (AIRO), a weekly-updated dashboard of catastrophic-risk forecasts from an ensemble of frontier AI models. Current ensemble forecasts for an AI catastrophe killing at least 10% of the global population: 0.47% by 2030 and 6% by 2050. The team emphasizes the dashboard is a prototype and forecasts are tentative, with links to the dashboard and white paper.

entry.title: Solaris, an interface world model (folaris flavor) https://t.co/OvsBVibkQ9
entry.summary: Cristóbal Valenzuela announces or shares Solaris, described as an interface world model with a folaris flavor, linking to a demo.

entry.title: No matter how much you are hearing about AI, today is the least you will ever hear about AI.
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick observes that regardless of current AI coverage levels, today is the minimum amount of AI discourse people will ever experience, implying adoption and discussion will only grow.

entry.title: @SethCronin Chess, go, and math are highly constrained, purely cognitive that allow exact simulation...
entry.summary: Gary Marcus restates his long-running thesis that AI excels in constrained, purely cognitive domains like chess, go, and math (where exact simulation and formal verification apply) but remains weak in the open-ended physical world, warning that pushing cognitive techniques into robotics without solving alignment would be dangerously reckless.

entry.title: 🔎 New blog: day-0 support gets a model running in vLLM. From there, the community keeps making it fa...
entry.summary: The vLLM project highlights a new blog by AMD and EmbeddedLLM documenting how MiniMax M3 was optimized on Instinct MI355X GPUs after day-0 vLLM support: following the bottleneck to achieve 3-4x serving throughput gains, with reusable performance-tuning tips for future model optimization.

entry.title: @CahlDee From my understanding, he’s spent the last few years mostly focused on pre-training, which ...
entry.summary: Clement Delangue responds to criticism, explaining that a researcher in question has focused mostly on pre-training rather than AI risks, and clarifies his goal is not to discredit anyone but to put perspectives in context and listen to the broader AI ecosystem.

entry.title: Deepmind founders were in groups that made a concerted effort to make "AI existential risks" discour...
entry.summary: Gebru claims DeepMind founders belonged to groups that deliberately mainstreamed AI existential-risk discourse, saying such views were once dismissed in research spaces but proponents organized and raised billions.

entry.title: “right now, AI companies are underinvesting in safety” might prove to be the understatement of the c...
entry.summary: Gary Marcus argues that the statement that AI companies are underinvesting in safety may be the understatement of the century, implying the shortfall is far worse than commonly stated.

entry.title:
Yep. And then OpenAI decide to impair monitoring. Terrible idea.
And the White House said *nothing....
entry.summary: Gary Marcus criticizes OpenAI for a decision to impair monitoring/oversight, calling it a terrible idea, and notes that the White House has remained silent on the matter while crediting Senator Blumenthal for raising questions.

entry.title: @bharatkr All of the above + social scientists, other AI builders, futurists, investors, policymaker...
entry.summary: Hugging Face CEO Clement Delangue argues that discussions of AI should include a broad range of voices — social scientists, AI builders, futurists, investors, and policymakers — extending a prior point about whose expertise should be heard on AI risk.

entry.title: Enterprises can now create their own bespoke frontier models by licensing state of the art Runway mo...
entry.summary: Runway announces enterprise model licensing: companies can license state-of-the-art Runway model weights, fine-tune on their own data, self-host on their infrastructure, and commercialize results, supported by white-glove service and Forward Deployed Researchers.

entry.title: There's something deeply philosophical about the importance of human understanding in a world where ...
entry.summary: Jerry Liu reflects on Terence Tao's letter about AI in mathematics, arguing the point is not that AI is bad but that it should complement rather than replace human understanding, and muses on how much understanding humans should retain versus offload to AI.

entry.title: One of the main issues with AI document parsing is that because no solution is 100% accuracy, it's h...
entry.summary: Jerry Liu (LlamaIndex) discusses the core problem in AI document parsing: since no parser is fully accurate, it is hard to detect misparsed pages such as misaligned tables or hallucinated values. He describes LlamaIndex's investment in calibrated confidence scores that correlate with parsing mode and page complexity, enabling human-in-the-loop review and automated fallback logic for document-heavy workflows, and promotes LlamaParse.

entry.title:
Fugu Max is live on Open Router! 🐡
Our learned multi-agent orchestration engine routes tasks across...
entry.summary: Sakana AI announces that Fugu Max, its learned multi-agent orchestration engine routing tasks across open-weight and specialized models, is live on OpenRouter, listing pricing of $2/$6 per 1M tokens, multimodal image/PDF input, web search, configurable reasoning, and function calling.

entry.title:
As far as I can tell Gavin Baker is just making stuff up.
Few if any of the people who left OpenAI ...
entry.summary: Gary Marcus disputes investor Gavin Baker's claim that people who left OpenAI returned, listing departing researchers such as Daniel Kokotajlo, Jan Leike, Ilya Sutskever and the Anthropic founders as evidence, and argues dismissing their integrity without evidence is wrong.

entry.title: I literally just told my teammate that I KNEW how this wording was playing into the apocalyptic AGI ...
entry.summary: Gebru reflects on using the term autonomous weapons in a Q&A, arguing the legal definition differs from the popular killer-robots framing and warning that AGI-doom advocates co-opt terminology to shift discourse.

category.term: Framing and terminology in AI policy

entry.title: If it is, Elon, you literally in your “summoning the demon” speech at MIT helped lay the groundwork ...
entry.summary: Marcus responds to Elon Musk, pointing out that Musk himself laid groundwork for AI-doom discourse in his 2014 'summoning the demon' speech at MIT, calling Musk's apparent reversal the most bizarre, self-unaware tweet he has seen and asking what happened to him.

Hand-writing agent instructions...
entry.summary: AlphaSignalAI summarizes a Google paper on skill evolution for agents (WikiSkill/EvoSkill): hand-written agent instruction files rot as tasks shift, and skills can instead be rewritten from rollout evidence. Key findings: keeping a private notebook behind skills (coach learns from history while the actor stays blind) lifted accuracy from 48.7 to 63.7, while letting the actor peek dropped it to 60.9; transferred skills beat self-made ones 70.2 to 63.4, but one transferred skill crashed a stronger model from 50.5 to 18.1. Conclusion: gate every skill like a model release; repo is public under Apache 2.0.

entry.title: We also ask LLMs how the risk of an AI-related catastrophe changes depending on AI capabilities. Mod...
entry.summary: The Future of Research Institute account describes a forecasting exercise in which LLMs predict how AI-related catastrophe risk varies with AI capability levels. Models first forecast the frontier score on the Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI) six months ahead, then forecast catastrophe outcomes conditional on above- or below-median capability trajectories. As of September 10, the median ensemble forecast put the frontier ECI at 176 by March 10, 2027, and when models assumed their own 75th-percentile capability outcome, their forecast of catastrophe by 2030 rose by an ensemble factor of 1.42 relative to unconditional forecasts.

entry.title: Social Summary: September 11, 2026
entry.summary:
Frontier-lab news dominated the day.

  • François Chollet sparked conceptual debate by defining 'symbolic learning' as parallel to deep learning; Ethan Mollick framed recent AI math proofs as the 'jagged frontier' in action
  • John Carmack offered sharp technical critique of NVIDIA's Jetson Thor for robotics, calling its 128 GB memory over-provisioned for available bandwidth
  • Safety discourse ran hot: an Anthropic researcher's public resignation went viral, with Nathan Lambert parsing the claims and Gary Marcus arguing existential-risk talk distracts from poor lab security
  • Clément Delangue claimed Chinese labs are '100x more open' than American labs, reigniting open-source debates; Logan Kilpatrick countered by touting Gemini 3.8 Cyber over Claude Mythos on cyber-defense benchmarks
  • Compute anxiety grew over reported Pentagon loan talks with Fluidstack, Microsoft tripling data-center capacity, and Matt Shumer warning the 'era of subsidized tokens is ending'
  • Google AI highlighted the complete male fruit fly connectome as a community milestone
entry.content:
Frontier-lab news dominated the day.

  • François Chollet sparked conceptual debate by defining 'symbolic learning' as parallel to deep learning; Ethan Mollick framed recent AI math proofs as the 'jagged frontier' in action
  • John Carmack offered sharp technical critique of NVIDIA's Jetson Thor for robotics, calling its 128 GB memory over-provisioned for available bandwidth
  • Safety discourse ran hot: an Anthropic researcher's public resignation went viral, with Nathan Lambert parsing the claims and Gary Marcus arguing existential-risk talk distracts from poor lab security
  • Clément Delangue claimed Chinese labs are '100x more open' than American labs, reigniting open-source debates; Logan Kilpatrick countered by touting Gemini 3.8 Cyber over Claude Mythos on cyber-defense benchmarks
  • Compute anxiety grew over reported Pentagon loan talks with Fluidstack, Microsoft tripling data-center capacity, and Matt Shumer warning the 'era of subsidized tokens is ending'
  • Google AI highlighted the complete male fruit fly connectome as a community milestone

Exceptionally high engagement: ~17.8k likes and 5.3M views.

entry.title: SITUATION BREWING: OpenAI confirmed that since completing Navier-Stokes it has made substantial prog...
entry.summary: Reportedly citing the New York Times, the post claims OpenAI confirmed that after completing work on the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem it has made substantial progress on a second Millennium Prize problem and is preparing to share results.

entry.title: What you are seeing in math right now is a consequence of the jagged frontier, and a precursor of wh...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick argues that current AI advances in mathematical proofs exemplify the jagged frontier: AI can produce superhuman proofs while being unable to do the human aspects of the math profession (mentoring, community stewardship, fostering love of the field). He warns that AI companies focusing on the flashiest task may undermine the perceived value of the rest of the profession, a pattern he expects to spread across fields.

entry.title: "Symbolic learning" is simply "machine learning" (automatically learn function x -> y given examples...
entry.summary: Francois Chollet defines symbolic learning as machine learning whose substrate is symbolic, yielding discrete, explicit, code-like learned representations, contrasted with parametric curve-fitting while still allowing numbers and probabilities.

It reportedly beats GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Opus 5 on several agentic, coding, and cyber benchmarks, outperforms the larger V4-Pro on most benchmarks, and is priced at $0.15/$0.60 per million input/output tokens, with V4.1-Pro still to come.

552...
entry.summary: vLLM announces day-0 serving of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, verified on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs. The post details the 552B MoE backbone with native vision and 1M context, dynamic activation (8B active reading, 16B writing), architecture carried over from V4 (hyper-connections, sliding-window plus compressed sparse attention, DSpark drafting, MXFP4 experts), and two novelties: Engram, 197B parameters of n-gram memory looked up rather than computed (a quarter of the checkpoint), and compressed KV written by only four layers with the rest sharing it.

entry.summary: Francois Chollet argues that symbolic learning, when correctly implemented, is directly parallel and comparable to deep learning, differing only in representation substrate and learning mechanism, and suggests the two approaches may eventually converge.

entry.title: A critical factor in using agents successfully in Codex and Code is deciding when & how to use t...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick discusses a key factor in successfully using coding agents like Codex: deciding when and how to steer them. He argues that failing to actively steer long-running agentic work means you are not managing agents sufficiently and should build interim reporting mechanisms for visibility during execution.

entry.title:
We've also added auto mode to Claude Managed Agents.
With `auto`, Claude reviews each tool call bas...
entry.summary: The official Claude developer account announces a new auto mode for Claude Managed Agents. In auto mode, Claude reviews each tool call against the user intent expressed in user.message events and autonomously decides whether to execute the tool call, deny it, or request user input. This adds a configurable supervision level to the agent framework, sitting between full manual approval and fully autonomous execution.

entry.title: Most diffusion-based video models are trained on short clips. When they’re used to relight longer vi...
entry.summary: NVIDIA AI announces HorizonRelight, a research collaboration with USC being presented at ECCV 2026. The work addresses a known limitation of diffusion-based video relighting models trained on short clips: when applied to longer videos in chunks, lighting visibly jumps at boundaries. The method propagates target-domain context between sliding windows to produce consistent lighting across long videos with fewer artifacts.
